svg.aria-label: Diagram: AWS Security Incident Response ingests findings from detection sources the customer already has rather than generating them, triages only threat detection findings and not security posture or compliance findings, escalates to the customer in less than one percent of ingested findings with no option to mute those notifications, accesses control plane logging only during an active investigation while never providing the log data back to customers, and publishes an explicit boundary list excluding threat hunting, forensic disk and endpoint analysis, recovery and remediation execution, attribution, legal guidance and custom reporting. Containment actions run on the customer's behalf only when pre-authorised, otherwise engineers provide manual guidance. Only accounts enrolled in the membership are monitored, and in the published RACI matrix the customer is Responsible for determining account scope, enabling AWS Organizations, selecting the delegated administrator and setting up membership details while the Security Incident Response team is Informed.
svg.title: It absorbs the findings and returns a conclusion, not the evidence
svg.text: A service judged by what it does not forward.
AWS Security Incident Response — “engages you only when action is required”. Aligned to NIST 800-61.
IN — findings you already produce
“doesn’t generate security findings. It ingests
findings from detection sources you already have”
Amazon GuardDuty · third party via Security Hub
So GuardDuty stays, and output quality is bounded
by what you already had.
NOT TRIAGED AT ALL
“only triages threat detection findings.
Security posture or compliance findings …
aren’t triaged”
A public bucket is a state, not a threat. That half
stays with Config, Security Hub or an SCP — silently.
The filter is the product, so the output is small and cannot be turned down
ESCALATION “less than 1% of ingested findings result in a customer-facing escalation”
MUTING “There’s no option to mute or suppress these notifications” → staff for it
A tool you cannot silence is one that has to be right. Suppression exists, but a suppressed finding is permanent.
OUT — the conclusion, not the evidence
“accesses control plane logging only during an
active investigation for the purpose of that
investigation. Log data isn’t provided to
customers.”
And enabling CloudTrail and VPC Flow Logs is
your listed responsibility. Your copy is the only one.
Containment is decided before the incident
“When pre-authorized, engineers execute
containment actions on your behalf”
runbooks: S3 buckets · EC2 instances · IAM
Otherwise: “engineers provide manual guidance”
Same engineers at 3am. Different outcome, settled
at onboarding.
The boundary list, read backwards, is your staffing plan
Threat hunting “threats that haven’t generated a detection finding” → you
Forensics “engineers perform log-based investigation only” → you
Remediation “Engineers provide recommendations only” → you
Attribution “the specific threat actor or group” → nobody
And the onboarding is yours: in the RACI matrix the customer is R, the SIR team is I.
Determine account scope · enable AWS Organizations · select the delegated administrator · set up membership
details. The triage is managed. Getting to the point where there is triage is not.
“Only you can close a case” — and if you do not reply, “the investigation might be placed on hold”. Both ways round.
